scope: Proposition 6.6 (Varying observed sets and filled values) of the manuscript “Uniform real Lipschitz surfaces on the triangular lattice” (preprints/Uniform-real-Lipschitz-surfaces-on-the-triangular-lattice-October-6-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 232 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dce5ae39087f446a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 43. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let Kn have the mesh thickness property with common constants and converge in Hausdorff distance to K. Let their mesh vertices carry random values zn, and let Un be random piecewise affine extensions on Q∗. Fix 3/2 < p < 2. Assume the following bounds, uniformly in n: 1. E∥Un∥W1,p ≤ C, and the means EUn have a subsequence converging strongly in Lp to u; 2. every vertex on Kn can be moved to a retained vertex on Kn within distance ℓn/n, where ℓn ≤ C(log n)C; 3. Un = zn at retained vertices, and their values satisfy Lemma 6.5 for some q > 3, with EEn ≤ C; 4. exceptional events in these assertions have vanishing contribution to the Sobolev, anchor, and fixed-scale averaged quantities used here. Then u has zero 1/2-Frostman trace on K and is zero Lebesgue-almost everywhere on K. If the original interpolated values also satisfy E∥zn − Un∥L1(Q) −→ 0, (6.6) then the original mean responses have the same distributional limit, including for smooth tests whose supports meet K.
